method: Only current competent first-party Church sources control publication. The Athens Archdiocese overview says it has 21 archiepiscopal regions, 146 parish churches, 12 cemetery churches, 9 monastic churches, and 158 chapels. Its current named rosters enumerate all of those groups except that the chapel page renders 155 named bodies. Those 155 are published and the three unnamed bodies remain held. Search engines, maps, historical projects, tourism sources, and aggregators remain discovery-only.

candidates.name: Three Athens Archdiocese chapels not named by the current roster
candidates.status: hold for exact identities from the competent source
candidates.reason: The official overview states 158 chapels, while the current official chapel page renders 155 named cards. The missing three are not inferred from search or map results.

candidates.name: Chapels, metochia, and outlying dependencies named inside Athens monastery profiles
candidates.reason: Several monastery profiles name dependent chapels and metochia, some outside the Archdiocese and some overlapping the chapel roster. They require exact body-by-body reconciliation before publication so one dependency is not manufactured twice.

candidates.name: Complete local body rosters for the remaining autocephalous metropolises of the Church of Greece
candidates.status: hold for current complete first-party metropolis rosters
candidates.reason: The central Church of Greece list establishes the competent metropolises already represented by parent rows. Athens is the current complete local roster published in this tranche. Other local bodies remain to be reconciled metropolis by metropolis.

candidates.name: Complete local rosters for the New Lands metropolises
candidates.status: hold for current complete first-party metropolis rosters
candidates.reason: The Ecumenical Patriarchate and Church of Greece already establish the New Lands parent sees and their administrative relationship. Their parish and monastery rosters remain a separate local first-party reconciliation.

candidates.name: Complete local rosters for the Church of Crete
candidates.status: hold for current complete first-party eparchial rosters
candidates.reason: The Ecumenical Patriarchate establishes the Church of Crete and its eparchies already represented by parent rows. Local parishes and monasteries remain to be reconciled from each competent eparchy.

candidates.name: Complete local rosters for the Dodecanese eparchies and the Patriarchal Exarchate of Patmos
candidates.status: hold for current complete first-party eparchial rosters
candidates.reason: The Ecumenical Patriarchate establishes the Dodecanese metropolises and Patmos already represented by parent rows. Their subordinate bodies require local official rosters.

candidates.name: Twenty ruling monasteries of Mount Athos and their current dependencies
candidates.status: hold for a complete current first-party Holy Community roster
candidates.reason: The existing directory represents the Holy Community. Search, tourism, government, heritage, and individual monastery sources confirm many identities but do not replace one current complete competent roster of all ruling monasteries and dependencies. No disputed or irregular Athonite body is inferred.

candidates.name: Additional canonical parallel bodies in Greece
candidates.status: hold for competent first-party confirmation and parent reconciliation
candidates.reason: The Athens chapel roster explicitly identifies several dependencies of Jerusalem, Sinai, Hydra, Gortys, Syros, and Megara, which are parented neutrally in the published tranche. Any further canonical parallel body must be tied to its own competent authority before publication.

candidates.name: Search and map discoveries not yet tied to a competent canonical source
candidates.reason: A public listing, map pin, social page, or historical directory does not establish current canonical identity or parentage. Such discoveries remain unpublished until a competent Church source verifies them.

source_reconciliations.subject: Athens official overview and rendered rosters
source_reconciliations.decision: The overview's 21 regions, 146 parishes, 12 cemetery churches, and 9 monastic bodies reconcile exactly to their current named pages. The chapel page renders 155 named cards rather than the overview's 158, so only 155 are published.

source_reconciliations.subject: Athens chapel parentage across canonical authorities
source_reconciliations.decision: Where the official chapel page expressly says a chapel belongs to a local parish, that parish is its parent. Dependencies it expressly assigns to Jerusalem, Sinai, Hydra, Gortys, Syros, or Megara retain those existing canonical parents. All others remain directly under the Athens Archdiocese.

source_reconciliations.subject: Body-level contact coverage
source_reconciliations.decision: Telephone numbers, email addresses, and body-owned websites are published only when printed by the official Archdiocese roster or the body's official Archdiocesan profile. Personal mobile numbers attached to named clergy are not republished. Each published contact carries its exact official source and check date. Four body-owned domains are printed by those profiles. Monipetraki and Zoodochos answered on the check date; Panagia Vryoulon had no resolving host, and Porphyrios did not present a usable HTTPS root. Those two domains remain identified as officially published contact information rather than being silently replaced by a third-party link.

source_reconciliations.subject: Duplicate-looking dedications
source_reconciliations.decision: Repeated dedications are not collapsed when the official source identifies different locations or institutions. The two Saint Andrew chapels with otherwise identical short titles are distinguished by the locations printed with their official entries.

official_jurisdiction_audit.result: The existing directory already carries the autocephalous parent sees. This tranche adds the current complete named Athens roster. The remaining local rosters stay bounded by metropolis.

The existing directory already carries Crete, the Dodecanese, Patmos, the New Lands, direct patriarchal monasteries, and Mount Athos at parent level. Their subordinate rosters remain held until competent first-party lists are reconciled.

official_jurisdiction_audit.jurisdiction: Jerusalem, Sinai, and other canonical dependencies
official_jurisdiction_audit.result: The Athens official chapel roster explicitly identifies several dependencies outside the Athens Archdiocese. The published rows retain those competent parents rather than being absorbed into the Church of Greece.
